title: What If 87 Feet of Rain Fell in One Year? In 1861 One Town Got It

scenes.text: What if it rained 87 feet in a single year? One town in India measured it.
Cherrapunji sits on a ridge in northeast India. Wet monsoon air from the Bay of Bengal hits the hills and is forced upward.
Between August 1860 and July 1861, about 26 and a half meters of rain fell. Still the world record.
In July 1861 alone, 9.3 meters. Thirty feet of rain in a month.
Even now it averages nearly 12 meters a year, and people cross rivers on bridges grown from living tree roots.
And the twist: in the dry winter, one of the wettest places on Earth runs short of drinking water.

description:
What if 87 feet of rain fell in one year? Between 1 August 1860 and 31 July 1861, Cherrapunji in Meghalaya, India, recorded about 26,470 millimeters, which Guinness World Records still lists as the greatest rainfall in a year.
July 1861 alone brought 9,300 millimeters, the record for a single month. Monsoon clouds from the Bay of Bengal cross the plains of Bangladesh and are forced to rise at the Khasi Hills. The town still averages about 11,777 millimeters a year, just behind nearby Mawsynram, and its valleys are crossed by living root bridges that take 10 to 15 years to grow. Yet in the dry winter months residents face water shortages and may walk long distances for drinking water.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: On 16 June 1995 the town got more than a meter and a half of rain in a single day. How much rain is too much for you? Drop your own what-if below.
